title: Forget RAG Pipelines—Build Production Ready Agents in 15 Mins: Nina Lopatina, Rajiv Shah, Contextual
talk_summary: A Contextual AI workshop demos a managed RAG platform: document parsing, hybrid retrieval/reranking, grounded generation, claim-level grounding checks, and natural-language unit-test evals. Most content is product marketing, but the eval, grounding, and retrieval mechanisms are copyable for agent review and context workflows.

takeaways.what_they_do: Define pass/fail criteria as natural-language unit tests, run them over a batch of prompts/responses, score each 1-5 with a judge model, aggregate by category, then change prompt/settings based on weak categories.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to create unit tests for the prompt that will ask specific questions that you want tested about those responses
takeaways.numbers: 1-5 scale; example score 2.2/5; six queries and six unit tests

takeaways.what_they_do: After generation, decompose output into individual claims and check each against retrieved source context; flag unsupported sentences to users.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to decompose that answer into specific claims... is this claim grounded back in that context or not

takeaways.what_they_do: Use BM25 plus embeddings to retrieve ~100 chunks, then an instruction-following reranker to select ~15 high-quality chunks; reranker prompt can prefer recency or other criteria.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our defaults are something like a hundred chunks that will come back... use a reranker... default is 15

takeaways.what_they_do: Reformulate ambiguous/abbreviated queries or split long complex queries into smaller subqueries, answer each, then synthesize.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take that query, break it up into smaller subqueries, answer each of those

takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap a RAG agent as a simple MCP server; the tool docstring tells clients what the agent covers, then clients like Claude/Cursor can call it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the important thing of course is that doc string that you kind of describe what your rag agent is about

takeaways.what_they_do: Attach rich metadata (created date, author/authority) to documents and use it at retrieval/generation to prefer recent or authoritative sources when documents conflict.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe this is the most recent or this was written by the authoritative person
